best_for: Discord users on Linux, especially on Wayland, who want screen sharing with sound and Vencord plugins, and accept that Discord does not endorse client mods.
description:
Vesktop is a custom desktop app for Discord, made by the team behind Vencord, the Discord client mod. You sign in with your normal Discord account and chat, call and join servers the same way. The team says Vesktop has no tracking or telemetry of its own and blocks Discord's telemetry out of the box.

Besides plugins, you can change how Discord looks with themes. Power users can trigger actions such as mute or push-to-talk from other programs with a command like `vesktop --run-shortcut toggleMute`, or from their window manager's own key bindings, so a single key can control Discord even when it sits in the background.

points.title: Screen share with audio on Linux
points.text: Screen sharing with sound works on Wayland. Global shortcuts such as push-to-talk work on Windows and X11, need Accessibility permission on macOS, and need a desktop with the GlobalShortcuts portal, such as GNOME or KDE, on Wayland.

points.title: Vencord comes built in
points.text: Vesktop is an unofficial Discord app with Vencord's plugins preinstalled; you switch on the ones you want. The project says it is lighter than the official app and gives Discord less access to your system.

points.title: Client mods break Discord's terms
points.text: Vencord's own FAQ says client modifications are against Discord's Terms of Service. It also says there are no known bans for using them and that the built-in plugins are safe. If your account matters a lot, the FAQ suggests not using mods.

points.title: Native packages beat the Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is verified as published by the Vencord team, in x64 and ARM64. Vesktop's Linux guide still prefers its .deb, .rpm, AUR or AppImage builds, because in the Flatpak rich presence does not work well and drag-and-drop needs access to all files.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: It is GPL-3.0 licensed, with no paid tier. Only vencord.dev and vesktop.dev are official, and the FAQ warns that other sites claiming to be official are likely malicious.

points.title: Rolling back on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 26 versions of the 64-bit installer. macOS (universal, macOS 13 or later) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
